The top is a flame on a small brazier cup that ends flat on the thin shaft, like a hat. The cup is not an ellipse plate with narrower rows above and below. styleAnswer.evidence: The torch post is a thin prop, so the per-tile tone count of 0 is not held against it; I judged density by eye. The post and the grey base block read as nearly flat fills with about 3 lightness steps. The measured near-flat coverage is 19%, while the thin references (bench, lamp, hedge, well) all sit at 0% and the stall at 13%. The bench and lamp-crook show per-piece grain and highlight/shadow banding that the candidate lacks. Only 19 distinct colours cover the flame, post and base, so the post looks flatter and more sticker-like than the lamp-crook or bench beside it. Dark edge pixels are 38% neutral, so the outline is partly tinted and partly neutral (mixed). The flame is small, with only a couple of tones. A careful artist would not accept it next to the references without more wood grain, base stone shading and highlights.
